application.name: ofetch
application.summary: A lightweight, type-safe fetch wrapper for making HTTP requests.
application.purpose: Provide a small client-side/server-side HTTP client with retries, timeouts, hooks, response parsing and typed errors, exportable for browsers and Node.js.

domains.name: HTTP client core
domains.description: Core request execution: option resolution, URL/query handling, body serialization, response parsing, retry logic and error dispatch.

domains.name: Error handling
domains.description: Normalized FetchError creation with request/response/data accessors and retry-aware throwing.

domains.name: Options and hooks
domains.description: Resolving defaults/options, merging headers, building query/params and invoking lifecycle hooks.

domains.name: Response processing
domains.description: Detecting and parsing response types (json/text/blob/stream/arrayBuffer) from content-type and parseResponse overrides.

domains.name: Runtime integration
domains.description: Browser/universal entry and Node entry with optional keep-alive agent.

domains.name: Examples and testing
domains.description: Example type-safety demo, playground and test harness exercising the library.

entityAnnotations.businessMeaning: Core factory that builds a type-safe fetch client with default/global options, retry logic, hooks and response parsing.
Handles request failure: decides retries (skipping aborts and payload-method retries by default), waits, then throws a normalized FetchError.
Builds a normalized FetchError with a formatted message and lazy accessors for request, options, response, data and status fields.
Merges input options, global defaults, headers and query/params into resolved options for a request.
Merges request/default headers into a Headers instance (defaults overridden by input).
Executes a single or array of lifecycle hooks sequentially.
Determines whether an HTTP method carries a request body (PATCH/POST/PUT/DELETE) and should not be retried by default.
Decides whether a request body should be auto-serialized as JSON/form-urlencoded or passed through (e.g. FormData, URLSearchParams, streams, binary).
Infers the response parsing mode (json/text/stream/blob) from the content-type header.
Node-specific fetch setup; returns keep-alive agent-aware fetch when FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE is enabled, otherwise the platform/native fetch.
Demo of typed response consumption (repo object strongly typed).
Manual smoke test hitting an error endpoint and printing/catching the result.
Test helper verifying that an aborted request is not retried.

applicationFacts: Dual entry points: src/index.ts (universal/browser) and src/node.ts (Node), both built from a shared createFetch core.
Uses destr for JSON parsing, ufo for URL joining (withBase/withQuery) and headless request/response handling.
Default retry set is 408/409/425/429/500/502/503/504; payload methods are not auto-retried and abort errors bypass retry.
JSON bodies are auto-serialized (JSON.stringify or URLSearchParams for form-urlencoded) with content-type/accept headers set.
Response bodies are parsed based on content-type (json/text/blob/stream/arrayBuffer) or an explicit responseType/parseResponse override.
The library supports hooks around request, request-error, response and response-error phases, with single or array hooks.
Errors thrown are FetchError instances that expose request, options, response, data, statusCode/statusMessage and status/statusText.
Test suite spins up a real local h3 server to exercise ok/params/url/echo/post/binary/403/408/204/timeout endpoints.
